question: Which pretraining-data properties make memorized factual knowledge extractable by later question-answer fine-tuning?

key_findings.claim: Token-level memorization of a biography does not guarantee that later instruction tuning can extract its facts.
key_findings.evidence: GPT-style models reach over 99% pretraining first-token accuracy and can fit QA for half the people, yet achieve essentially zero OOD QA on the other half across LoRA/full fine-tuning, model sizes up to 682M, and hundreds of data passes.

key_findings.claim: Paraphrase multiplicity, sentence permutation, and repeated entity names during pretraining make facts far more extractable.
key_findings.evidence: On synthetic biographies, five diverse and shuffled entries per person raise OOD QA accuracy from 9.7% to 96.6%; mixed BIO+QA training also reaches 86.6%/77.7% on synthetic/rewritten datasets.

key_findings.claim: Nearly linear probes correlate extraction with whether attributes become available at the entity-name representation.
key_findings.evidence: P-probing and Q-probing show unaugmented models reveal attributes only after their textual occurrence or related attributes, whereas heavily augmented models predict them from the person's name; QA and Q-probe accuracies track closely.

key_findings.claim: Augmenting a related celebrity subset can improve extraction for non-augmented minority biographies.
key_findings.evidence: Adding an augmented 100k-person celebrity group during pretraining raises minority QA accuracy from 4.4% to 86.8% on bioS and from 10.0% to 76.3% on bioR, despite unchanged minority text and no minority QA fine-tuning.

method.core_idea: Pretrain controlled GPT/Llama-style models on synthetic or Llama-rewritten biographies, vary knowledge augmentation, and test OOD QA plus representation probes.
method.mechanism: Each of 100k people has six independent attributes; QA tuning sees only half the entities, while P/Q probes freeze the transformer and use a small embedding update plus linear classifier to locate encoded attributes.
assumptions: Synthetic biographies and six attributes capture mechanisms relevant to web-scale factual learning.
Exact-match QA and near-linear probe accuracy measure usable parametric knowledge.
Repeated data passes and from-scratch 124M-682M models are informative about industrial one-pass pretraining.

techniques.role: Separates extracting facts from memorizing the same questions.
Varies paraphrases, order, name repetition, and mixed QA exposure.
Tests where factual attributes become linearly accessible.

evaluations.setting: 100k synthetic bioS and Llama-rewritten bioR people
evaluations.result: Unaugmented pretrain-then-finetune often fails despite BIO fit; five-entry diversity reaches 96.6% in a highlighted bioS setting.
evaluations.baseline: Single-biography pretraining, mixed BIO+QA training, LoRA and full fine-tuning

evaluations.metric: Attribute classification from frozen hidden states
evaluations.result: Early/name-only linear accessibility grows with augmentation and closely correlates with QA extraction.
evaluations.baseline: Probe positions after attributes and unaugmented pretrained models

evaluations.metric: Minority OOD QA and attribute-specific extraction
evaluations.result: Related augmented celebrity text transfers strongly; bidirectional MLM still fails on many multiword attributes and favors locally associated words.
evaluations.baseline: No celebrity group and autoregressive models

limitations: The controlled facts are templated, independent, and repeated far more than most web facts; model scale stops below 1B in this paper.
Probe training includes an embedding update, so 'linear encoding' is approximate rather than a parameter-free readout.
Diversity can introduce extra tokens, optimization steps, or entity mentions; industrial rewriting benefits and factual faithfulness are not evaluated.
failure_modes: A model memorizes surface sequences while binding an attribute to nearby words rather than the entity key.
Later QA tuning cannot reorganize inaccessible stored facts even when it fits seen entities.
Automatic rewriting may distort rare facts, amplify bias, or waste pretraining compute.
reusable_insights: Factual-memory experiments should hold entities, not merely prompt templates, out of QA training.
Measure accessibility separately from token reconstruction or perplexity.
Data-diversity interventions need controls for multiplicity, order, key repetition, and total compute.
open_questions: Do one-pass billion-scale pretraining mixtures exhibit the same binding and accessibility transitions?
Can early hidden-state or gradient diagnostics predict extractability before expensive QA fine-tuning?
How can rewriting maximize binding diversity while guaranteeing semantic and provenance fidelity?

competitive_landscape.title: Language Models as Knowledge Bases?
competitive_landscape.difference: LAMA demonstrates factual recall in internet-pretrained models but cannot exclude exposure to equivalent queries; this paper uses entity-held-out controlled pretraining and QA.

competitive_landscape.title: Knowledge Neurons in Pretrained Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Knowledge Neurons attributes facts to feed-forward activations in pretrained models; this work studies name-token accessibility and its causal dependence on pretraining data diversity.

competitive_landscape.title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT
competitive_landscape.difference: ROME localizes and edits existing subject-relation associations; this paper asks which training distributions make an association extractable at all and uses controlled from-scratch corpora.

competitive_landscape.title: Mass-Editing Memory in a Transformer
competitive_landscape.difference: MEMIT edits many facts post hoc; the reviewed work changes pretraining presentation so downstream tuning can retrieve originally learned facts.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: factual probing and causal memory localization were established. The distinctive contribution is a controlled separation of sequence memorization from entity-held-out extraction, linked quantitatively to augmentation and name-centered near-linear accessibility.
reviewer_notes: Main text and relevant appendices were checked, including exact data construction, training exposure, negative results, probe parameterization, celebrity transfer, and GBERT. Primary competitor records checked 2026-08-23. Claims about industrial rewriting remain extrapolations from controlled sub-billion-scale experiments.
